newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends higher despite heavy farm selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends higher despite heavy farm selling.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed higher on local and commercial buying sparked by the strength of CBOT soybeans which helped absorb heavy hedge selling as farmers sold into the rally, floor sources said.
Crushers were also featured buyers late, helping the market to close just below the day's highs.

Japan was reported to have bought 3,000 to 4,000 tonnes of Canadian canola overnight. Dealers said export demand may have been greater but for the current strength of the Canadian dollar versus the yen.
Flaxseed closed mostly higher, boosted by commercial buying and gains in other oilseed markets. March flax finished unchanged at $362.00.
Feed wheat futures closed lower on local and commercial selling linked to concern about abundant feed supplies across Western Canada. March ended $3.70 lower at $172.30.
Western barley also finished lower with February off $0.60 at $136.40.
Activity was sparse in oats and feed peas.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
